# Synthetic HEVC decoder fixtures

These pictures were generated by `modules/codec/tests/hevc_decode_fixture.cpp`
with Apple's VideoToolbox on a physical Apple Silicon Mac (macOS 27.0.1,
Xcode 27.1, 2026-10-24). They contain only this repository's synthetic luma
gradient/checker pattern and neutral chroma, under the project's license.

The decoder tests read these samples instead of asking the current machine to
encode them. Hosted virtual Macs can encode ordinary Main/Main10 tiles while
their advertised encoder fails on monochrome or other extended profiles.
The production encoder still has its separate live VideoToolbox tests.

The corpus preserves all 56 profile/range/size roundtrips, two explicit chroma
locations, and the large 4:2:2 tile used by cancellation/progress tests. The same
512-pixel sample also drives the 61MP decode-memory test. Pixel comparisons,
the 40 dB PSNR threshold, malformed-sample checks and 512 KB stacks are unchanged.

Each `.bin` holds the five-byte magic `HDRVT`, version byte 1, a four-byte
big-endian hvcC length, the hvcC record, and one length-prefixed HEVC picture.
The input pixels are reconstructed independently of decoding from the helper's
fixed pattern; uncompressed pictures are not stored. `SHA256SUMS` records the
committed corpus.

To regenerate on a physical Mac with support for all profiles:

```sh
DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer \
  cmake --build build --target hevc_vt_decode_test
HYPERDR_RECORD_HEVC_FIXTURES=1 \
  ctest --test-dir build -R '^hevc_vt_decode(_memory)?_test$' --output-on-failure
ctest --test-dir build -R '^hevc_vt_decode(_memory)?_test$' --output-on-failure
```

Regeneration must pass both the live-encode run and the recorded-sample replay.
Update `SHA256SUMS` after intentionally regenerating the corpus.
